newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bourse freezes rise of five small shares.
newsitem.headline: Manila bourse freezes rise of five small shares.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) froze on Wednesday the share prices of five small-cap counters after they have reached the 50 percent ceiling or close to it.
The issues frozen were Pacifica Inc, Imperial Resources Inc A, Itogon Suyoc Mines Inc A and B, Marsteel Consolidated Inc A and B and Fil-Hispano Ceramics Inc A.
The PSE automatically freezes prices of issues when they rise by or close to 50 percent within a single trading day. The shares can then only be traded at or below the frozen price.

The rise in shares of oil company Pacifica was stopped at 3.70 centavos after it climbed by 48 percent. Also frozen was another oil counter, Imperial Resources A, which rose 50 percent to 9.75 centavos.
For the fifth straight session, Itogon A and B shares were frozen at 24.50 centavos, a 48.48 percent jump from 16.50 centavos.
The prices of holding firm Marsteel A and B was halted at six centavos from four centavos, a 50 pecent jump.
Fil-Hispano Ceramics A shares were frozen after rising 50 percent from 20 pesos to 30 pesos.
The PSE surveillance department said that it has written to the companies to explain the climb in their share prices.
Of the five, only Itogon submitted an advisory on Wednesday that its board had decided to change the stock's par value from one centavo to one peso.
Traders said rumours of backdoor listings and buy-ins may have encouraged the heavy buying in thirdliner issues since late last week.

"They are just being played, which happens sometimes when blue chips are quiet and rumours about thirdliner issues circulate. There is some truth sometimes to the rumours but more often they are just that, rumours," Felix Barrientos, a dealer at ING Barings, said.
